evals.name: fresh-machine-full-configure
evals.prompt: I just installed JAIBA on a new laptop. Can you configure it for me?

context.host: vendor identity not determinable from the running agent

evals.expected_output: Runs the greeting banner. Identifies the host agent by self-introspection (not by scanning any repo); unable to resolve a vendor, falls back to the neutral ~/.agents/ as the global config root and says why. Installs assets/jaiba-contract.md as ~/.agents/jaiba-contract.md and wires a reference from the vendor's global instructions file if one exists. Checks `npx skills list -g`, installs the missing skillset.txt entries at the chosen scope, then copies the subagent battery from assets/agents/ (executor-high/medium/low, code-analyst, business-analyst, verify) into ~/.agents/agents/. Creates NOTHING inside any repository — no .ai/, no .atl/, no AGENTS.md. Closing report covers host + config root, contract, skills, battery, and names jaiba-init as the next step for setting up a specific project without invoking it.

evals.name: project-intent-hands-off-to-jaiba-init
evals.prompt: Set up JAIBA for this repo I'm working on.
evals.expected_output: Performs only the global work: contract into ~/.claude/jaiba-contract.md, skillset install, subagent battery into ~/.claude/agents/. Does not create the .ai/ skeleton, the .atl/ directory, or an AGENTS.md marker in the repo, and does not invoke update-brain or jaiba-doctor. Closes by telling the developer that the machine is configured and that the repo-scoped setup is `jaiba-init`, to be run from inside that repo — a mention, not an invocation.

evals.name: rerun-on-already-configured-machine
evals.prompt: I upgraded jaiba, re-run the configure to refresh my setup.

context.global_config_state: ~/.claude/jaiba-contract.md is byte-identical to the packaged assets/jaiba-contract.md; all six subagent definitions present and identical; every skillset.txt entry already in `npx skills list -g`

evals.expected_output: Does NOT refuse to re-run — global configuration is refreshable by design. Compares each artifact against the packaged version, finds everything current, installs and overwrites nothing, and reports each item as 'already current'. Applies Case A for skills: nothing installed, developer pointed at `npx skills update -g`. Closing report states plainly that the machine was already up to date.

evals.name: all-skillset-skills-already-global

context.global_skills_state: every skill listed in skills/jaiba-configure/assets/skillset.txt (conduct, ask, fast, update-brain, create-knowledge, jaiba-doctor, caveman) is already present in `npx skills list -g` output
context.global_config_state: no jaiba-contract.md, no agents/ definitions yet

evals.expected_output: Before installing anything, ran `npx skills list -g` and found every skillset.txt entry already global. Installed no skills -- not globally, not project-locally. Told the developer their global skillset is complete and pointed them at `npx skills update -g` to stay current. Still performed the other global installs: the behavioral contract into the global config root and the subagent battery into its agents/ folder. Closing report explicitly notes Case A (already global, nothing installed).

evals.name: missing-skills-offered-global-or-local
evals.prompt: Install the jaiba skillset for me.

context.global_skills_state: `npx skills list -g` returns only jaiba-configure -- none of the skillset.txt entries (conduct, ask, fast, update-brain, create-knowledge, jaiba-doctor, caveman) are global yet

evals.expected_output: Ran `npx skills list -g`, found none of the skillset.txt entries present, and asked the developer ONCE -- before installing anything -- whether the missing skills should be installed globally (`npx skills add -y <source> --skill <skill> -g`, the recommended scope) or project-locally (same command without `-g`). Did not install anything before getting an answer. After the developer answers, installs only the missing entries one by one with the chosen scope, then installs the subagent battery.

evals.name: project-local-choice-targets-current-directory
evals.prompt: Yes, install the missing ones locally for the project I'm in.

context.prior_turn: jaiba-configure already ran `npx skills list -g` and found conduct, ask already global, but fast, update-brain, create-knowledge, jaiba-doctor, and caveman missing -- and just asked the developer global vs. project-local for the missing ones
context.cwd: a repo with a .claude/ directory at its root

evals.expected_output: Resolved the project-local target from the current working directory: .claude/ exists at its root, so skills go to .claude/skills/. Installed only the previously-missing skills (fast, update-brain, create-knowledge, jaiba-doctor, caveman) without -g, one by one. Did not reinstall or duplicate conduct or ask, which were already global. Then installed the contract and the subagent battery GLOBALLY regardless of the project-local skills choice — those are never project-scoped. Created no .ai/, .atl/ or AGENTS.md in that repo. Closing report distinguishes which skills came from where.

evals.name: existing-drifted-global-contract

context.global_agent_config: ~/.claude/ already holds a jaiba-contract.md from an older framework version (content differs from the packaged assets/jaiba-contract.md)

evals.expected_output: During step 2, detected the existing global jaiba-contract.md differs from the packaged version. Did NOT silently overwrite the machine-wide file: asked the developer whether to update (back up theirs, install the packaged version) or keep theirs (noting jaiba-doctor will keep flagging the drift). Proceeded with the skillset and subagent battery either way, and the closing report records which choice was made.

evals.name: drifted-subagent-definition

context.global_config_state: ~/.claude/agents/executor-high.md exists but was hand-edited by the developer; the other five definitions are identical to the packaged ones

evals.expected_output: Skipped the five identical subagent definitions as already current and did not overwrite the hand-edited executor-high.md: asked first, offering to back theirs up before installing the packaged version. Same non-destructive policy as the contract. Reports which definitions were skipped, which were installed, and what the developer chose for the drifted one.
